title: Cross-CPU portability sweep on AVX2-only dev host (AVX-512 deferred to f8d230ef)
description:
Run the `permanent_bipedal3` SIMD path on the dev host (AVX2-only) and document throughput + correctness. The AVX-512 throughput row is scoped out of this issue and tracked in follow-up `f8d230ef` (sibling under `7f809931`'s SIMD-and-platform-expansion epic).

## Background

The SIMD kernel (T12 / `686ee1b5`) compiles an AVX2 backend; the dev host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, Zen 3) has AVX2 only and no AVX-512 hardware was available within S3's measurement window. The scope of S3 is therefore the AVX2-only baseline on the dev host. The AVX-512 zmm bipedal-3 kernel and its throughput vs AVX2 are the deliverable of `f8d230ef`.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] Throughput measurements exist for the AVX2-only dev host at $n \in \{24, 28, 32, 36\}$. (Original criterion 1's AVX-512 row is delegated to `f8d230ef`.)
- [ ] [hard] Correctness equivalence: same seeded inputs produce bit-identical permanents across scalar, AVX2, and any locally-detected wider SIMD backends on the dev host. (Cross-host equivalence is delegated to `f8d230ef`.)
- [ ] [hard] CSV at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s3_cross_cpu-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` records mean wall-clock for the dev host with `lscpu`-style fingerprint.
- [ ] [hard] Writeup at `dev/plans/s3_cross_cpu_portability.md` exists, attached via `jit doc add`. The writeup records the AVX2-only baseline, explicitly cites `f8d230ef` for the deferred AVX-512 row, and documents the host-availability constraint that scoped this issue.
- [ ] [aspirational] AVX2 throughput improvement vs the scalar fallback is recorded as a sanity row in the CSV (confirms the SIMD path is actually being dispatched).

## Amendment history (2026-05-12)

S3's scope was amended 2026-05-12 to match dev-host hardware availability (AVX2-only). The deferred AVX-512 throughput row moved to a dedicated follow-up issue `f8d230ef` under `7f809931`. Full narrative + criterion mapping in `dev/active/363556e6-amendments-2026-05-12.md`.
